hero.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to JFK route in September, citing low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates, noting that air carriers fluctuate based on demand. JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying "It's easy. It's close." The route was viewed as a significant development for the Treasure Coast when it launched, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports.

Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said that route is performing well, noting "Boston is seeing great demand." The contrast between the two routes highlights how market conditions can vary significantly even for flights from the same regional airport to different Northeast destinations. Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future, explaining that JetBlue will evaluate the market continuously and that just because the route is gone now does not mean it will never come back.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs low-altitude Blue Angels flyover at Pensacola beach as safety review halted
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended a low-altitude Blue Angels flyover that scattered beach chairs and tents at a crowded Pensacola beach Wednesday, marking the third time he has intervened to halt safety investigations of controversial military flight maneuvers. Video circulating on social media showed a Navy demonstration jet flying so low over beachgoers that sand kicked up and children covered their ears as equipment went flying. The Navy initially announced it would conduct a thorough safety review following the incident. However, acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump administration appointee, posted on social media Thursday that the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. Hegseth retweeted the post and wrote on his personal account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell added "Carry on Patriots" alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above beachgoers. Navy officials would not confirm whether a routine flight debrief constituted the thorough safety review promised the day before. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing beachgoers photographing a Blue Angels jet with the words "Freedom" and "It's okay to love America."

Aviation safety experts criticized the administration's response. Jeff Guzzetti, a former crash investigator for the National Transportation Safety Board and Federal Aviation Administration, said it is shocking that top military leaders would excuse reckless behavior. Guzzetti warned that a cavalier attitude can only lead to accidents and noted that low-altitude flyovers have been linked to past crashes. Former Transportation Department Inspector General Mary Schiavo, also a pilot, said while such maneuvers may not violate military rules, the dangerous demonstrations performed by teams like the Blue Angels are not something to be performed over people. Guzzetti added that excusing unprofessional and dangerous behavior sends a powerful signal that such conduct is acceptable and desired, calling it the antithesis of a good safety culture.

The Pensacola incident follows two similar cases where Hegseth ended safety investigations. In March, he lifted suspensions of Army helicopter pilots who hovered near Kid Rock's Tennessee home, ending that investigation with no punishment and writing "Carry on, patriots." In July, he intervened again after South Carolina National Guard Apache pilots were suspended for a low-flying sweep over beachgoers during a July 4 event. In both cases, Hegseth used similar language ordering pilots to carry on. The NTSB sharply criticized the Army last year during investigation of a midair collision near Washington, finding the Army's aviation safety system failed to consistently detect and address hazards. In April 2025, a Japanese woman was killed after propeller wash from an Air Force helicopter knocked her down, with investigators noting an operational mindset fostering false confidence of safety.

cards.headline: Leon County jury orders Florida Rep. Fabian Basabe to pay $450,000 in sexual harassment case
cards.teaser: A Leon County jury found Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation, ordering him to pay $450,000 to former legislative aides and a parent.
cards.body:
Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe ended the week facing a $450,000 civil judgment after a Leon County jury found him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The case was brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother. Basabe represented himself despite having no legal training, and the trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders. Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told him that if an attorney had done half of what you had done, they would have been sanctioned, sir.

Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. After the verdict, however, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake. Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations. He has not been criminally charged, and an outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation. Basabe is seeking reelection this fall, and the verdict could also renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.body:
Demolition has begun at Murray Middle School in Martin County as the district moves forward with a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage from Hurricane Milton. The project includes rebuilding buildings destroyed by the tornadoes, along with construction of a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a complete parking lot overhaul. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, with the total project cost not yet finalized. The project is being funded through local capital improvement, sales tax, and Public Education Capital Outlay.

According to Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, the school was already scheduled for construction work before the hurricane hit. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Gernaine. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on." The tornado damage allowed the district to incorporate repairs to the three destroyed buildings into the expanded project that was already planned.

Students displaced from the affected classrooms continue to learn in portable classrooms during construction and will remain there until the work is complete. Barriers have been placed around the work zone to keep students away from the construction area. The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during the renovation process, with safety measures already in place to separate students from active construction zones.

The Martin County School District hopes to complete all renovations by December 2027. The reconstruction includes both the tornado damage repairs to buildings 18, 10, and 9, as well as the previously planned improvements to the administration area, media center, and art facilities. The comprehensive project represents a significant investment in the school's infrastructure, combining necessary storm repairs with long-term facility upgrades that were in the planning stages before Hurricane Milton struck the area.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major I-95 Ramp Closures Planned July 19-24
cards.teaser:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department
cards.body:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report highlights multiple full road and ramp closures expected to have the greatest impact on drivers.

## Major closures to know about

### Southbound I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Motorists will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt-Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. FDOT has scheduled July 26-30 as contingency dates in case the work is delayed by weather or other unforeseen conditions.

### Martin Highway ramps closing at I-95

Two ramps serving Martin Highway at I-95 will close overnight from **Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to Martin Highway at Exit 110 will be closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Drivers will continue north to Becker Road at Exit 114, travel west on Becker Road and use southbound I-95 to return to the Martin Highway exit.

The northbound I-95 entrance ramp from Martin Highway will also be closed during the same hours. Motorists will be detoured east on Martin Highway, north on Newfield Parkway and west on Becker Road to reach the northbound I-95 entrance ramp.

FDOT said only one ramp closure will occur at a time.

### Orange Avenue exit closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Drivers will be detoured to the eastbound Orange Avenue exit, north on Jenkins Road and west on Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are scheduled for July 26-30.

### Emergency repairs could cause major delays on I-95

Southbound I-95 between Kanner Highway and Bridge Road will have **two lanes closed beginning at 4 p.m. Monday, July 20, and Tuesday, July 21.** The lanes are scheduled to reopen by 5:30 a.m. each morning.

FDOT said the closures are needed to complete an emergency repair near mile marker 98. Drivers are encouraged to consider alternate routes because the early closure time could affect the evening commute.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads may close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several roads near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project. Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 20, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 24,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. Adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained throughout the work.

Detours will use nearby roads including SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and SW McDevitt Avenue. FDOT is also providing advance notice that SW Paar Drive between SW McIntosh Street and SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard may close from July 27-31.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Northbound and southbound I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line will continue to have two lanes closed overnight for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

U.S. 1 between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue may have two lanes closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times Monday through Friday for pavement widening and drainage work. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday for milling and resurfacing.

In Stuart, two westbound lanes on Monterey Road between Ocean Boulevard and Monterey Commons Boulevard may close from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday through Thursday.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during daytime and overnight hours.

SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard will have intermittent lane closures from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road will continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures as part of the widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions continue

Boaters traveling near the North Causeway Bridge in Fort Pierce could encounter partial or full channel closures as crews continue removing sections of the former drawbridge.

Partial channel restrictions may occur during daylight hours on weekdays through late 2026. At least 45 feet of the channel is expected to remain open during partial closures.

Intermittent full channel closures lasting up to six hours may occur through July for the removal of steel bascule bridge spans. Vessels requiring full channel access must provide the bridge tender with 120 minutes of advance notice.

The new North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, although nearby roads including U.S. 1, Old Dixie Highway, Juanita Avenue and Harbortown Drive may have lane restrictions.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

I-95 near the new Oslo Road interchange may have one or two lanes closed overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for roadway construction.

Drivers near Sebastian Inlet should expect intermittent lane and shoulder closures on A1A from July 20-31. Flaggers will direct traffic through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park remain closed during construction of the replacement bridge, although the park, boat ramp and portions of both parking areas remain open.

## Additional I-95 closures coming the following week

FDOT is also providing advance notice of several closures scheduled to begin Sunday, July 26. All four I-95 ramps at Midway Road are expected to close separately overnight through July 31 for paving. Only one ramp will close at a time.

Detours will use St. Lucie West Boulevard, U.S. 1 and nearby interstate exits. Additional ramp closures are also planned later at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway.

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Drivers should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through [Florida 511](https://fl511.com). Updated lane closure information is available through [FDOT District Four](https://www.fdot.gov/info/co/district4).

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement with crackdown on speeding
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is deploying additional deputies this summer to reduce speeding and reckless driving. Deputies have conducted more than 1,000 traffic stops in four weeks.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said she recently stopped someone doing 105 mph on I-95. Rodrigues stopped a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, Rodrigues stopped a driver going 73 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. Del Toro eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County man leads Martin County deputies on 100 mph chase through Indiantown
hero.body:
A Palm Beach County man led Martin County deputies on a high-speed chase through Indiantown after driving more than 100 mph on State Road 710, one of the area's most dangerous roads. Deputies spotted 33-year-old Markell Tillman driving aggressively at speeds exceeding 100 mph, forcing other vehicles off the roadway. When deputies attempted to stop him, Tillman fled. Tillman weaved through traffic in an attempt to lose deputies before turning onto SW Martin Highway toward Palm City, where he continued to drive recklessly.

Deputies spotted Tillman again traveling eastbound on Martin Highway near Allapattah Road. Deputies used stop sticks to disable his vehicle near I-95. Tillman then bailed out of the vehicle and attempted to flee on foot before deputies caught up with him and took him into custody. Tillman was arrested on charges of fleeing and eluding, aggravated fleeing with injury or damage, operating a vehicle exceeding the speed limit by 50 or more mph, driving while license suspended or revoked, obstruction without violence, and operating a vehicle at 100 or more mph. Tillman also had an out-of-county warrant at the time of his arrest. He was booked into the Martin County Jail.

hero.headline: Messi to face Yamal in World Cup final after bathing him as baby
hero.teaser: Photographer Joan Monfort's 2007 images of teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal for a charity calendar have gone viral before Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain.
hero.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing baby Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate. The infant was paired with Messi, who would become the greatest player of all time, while Yamal would become a star for Barcelona some 15 years later. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble, and Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when Spain won the title. Interest in the images has skyrocketed with the World Cup final approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media without credit or compensation. The 19-year-old Yamal will face Messi, who is 20 years his senior, when Spain plays Argentina in the World Cup final on Sunday in New Jersey. Monfort, 58, a lifelong Barcelona supporter, said his heart is split between wanting Messi or Yamal to win.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England 2-1 to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two late goals to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinal, with Enzo Fernandez equalizing in the 85th minute and Lautaro Martinez heading in the winner in stoppage time.
cards.body:
Argentina overcame a 1-0 deficit to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinal on Wednesday in Atlanta. England captain Harry Kane scored the opening goal in the 55th minute through Anthony Gordon, but Argentina rallied with goals from Enzo Fernandez in the 85th minute and substitute Lautaro Martinez in stoppage time. Lionel Messi assisted on both goals, feeding the ball to Fernandez for the equalizer from outside the box before sending in a cross for Martinez's header.

The defending champions will face European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team proved its collectiveness and brotherhood by fighting to the very end after falling behind. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more risk and rhythm, freeing them up while England played with a feeling they had a lot to lose.

Martinez said he told teammate Alexis Mac Allister before the game that he would come on and win it. The victory marked another occasion when Argentina has eliminated England at the World Cup, following games in 1986 and 1998. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as Argentina mounted wave after wave of attacks before breaking through.

cards.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent artificial intelligence from making game decisions
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make in-game decisions.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final at New Jersey stadium Sunday
cards.teaser: A sprawling network of federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies continue with a game plan two years in the making to ensure Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain is safe.
cards.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey will feature a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team monitoring the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything needed from a threat perspective.

The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says Trump's attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history.

cards.headline: Flip City gymnasts from Treasure Coast earn top 15 national finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three young gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine competed as one unit after advancing through local competitions, travel tournaments, states, and regionals during what Head Coach Candice Lazuka described as a strong season. The team came close to a perfect score at the national competition, achieving a 9.9.

The three gymnasts each came to the sport for different reasons. Rose-Daris said it wasn't really about gymnastics but rather the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan was drawn to gymnastics by watching gymnasts on YouTube and seeing how amazing they were and how fun it looked. Rine said she loves gymnastics because she learns new things. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world for the Junior Olympics. Supan described the opportunity as happy and exciting at the same time. Rine said she is focused on getting first place on floors at the upcoming competition.

hero.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs low-altitude Blue Angels flyover at Pensacola beach as safety review halted
hero.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended a low-altitude Blue Angels flyover that scattered beach chairs and tents at a crowded Pensacola beach Wednesday, marking the third time he has intervened to halt safety investigations of controversial military flight maneuvers. Video circulating on social media showed a Navy demonstration jet flying so low over beachgoers that sand kicked up and children covered their ears as equipment went flying. The Navy initially announced it would conduct a thorough safety review following the incident. However, acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump administration appointee, posted on social media Thursday that the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. Hegseth retweeted the post and wrote on his personal account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell added "Carry on Patriots" alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above beachgoers. Navy officials would not confirm whether a routine flight debrief constituted the thorough safety review promised the day before. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing beachgoers photographing a Blue Angels jet with the words "Freedom" and "It's okay to love America."

Aviation safety experts criticized the administration's response. Jeff Guzzetti, a former crash investigator for the National Transportation Safety Board and Federal Aviation Administration, said it is shocking that top military leaders would excuse reckless behavior. Guzzetti warned that a cavalier attitude can only lead to accidents and noted that low-altitude flyovers have been linked to past crashes. Former Transportation Department Inspector General Mary Schiavo, also a pilot, said while such maneuvers may not violate military rules, the dangerous demonstrations performed by teams like the Blue Angels are not something to be performed over people. Guzzetti added that excusing unprofessional and dangerous behavior sends a powerful signal that such conduct is acceptable and desired, calling it the antithesis of a good safety culture.

The Pensacola incident follows two similar cases where Hegseth ended safety investigations. In March, he lifted suspensions of Army helicopter pilots who hovered near Kid Rock's Tennessee home, ending that investigation with no punishment and writing "Carry on, patriots." In July, he intervened again after South Carolina National Guard Apache pilots were suspended for a low-flying sweep over beachgoers during a July 4 event. In both cases, Hegseth used similar language ordering pilots to carry on. The NTSB sharply criticized the Army last year during investigation of a midair collision near Washington, finding the Army's aviation safety system failed to consistently detect and address hazards. In April 2025, a Japanese woman was killed after propeller wash from an Air Force helicopter knocked her down, with investigators noting an operational mindset fostering false confidence of safety.

cards.headline: Leon County jury orders Florida Rep. Fabian Basabe to pay $450,000 in sexual harassment case
cards.teaser: A Leon County jury found Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation, ordering him to pay $450,000 to former legislative aides and a parent.
cards.body:
Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe ended the week facing a $450,000 civil judgment after a Leon County jury found him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The case was brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother. Basabe represented himself despite having no legal training, and the trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders. Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told him that if an attorney had done half of what you had done, they would have been sanctioned, sir.

Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. After the verdict, however, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake. Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations. He has not been criminally charged, and an outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation. Basabe is seeking reelection this fall, and the verdict could also renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action.

cards.headline: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon set for September trial on charges stemming from DeSantis office sit-in
cards.teaser: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office protesting Florida's congressional map.
cards.body:
Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. House. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave.

Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate. If they think the threat of a trial is going to make me back down, they picked the wrong woman, Nixon said following Wednesday's hearing. The trial is scheduled after Florida's Aug. 18 primary, in which Nixon is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination. Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million. Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Her campaign also promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup. Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term.

cards.headline: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback faces court hearing over Florida residency requirement
cards.teaser: A two-day hearing beginning July 21 will determine whether gubernatorial candidate James Fishback meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement after opponent Lt. Jay Collins challenged his eligibility.
cards.body:
Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will defend his eligibility to remain in the primary during a two-day hearing scheduled to begin Tuesday in Tallahassee. Lt. Jay Collins, one of Fishback's opponents, argues that records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida and maintained the state as his permanent home.

Because primary ballots have already been printed, the judge has said a ruling against Fishback could require election officials to post notices and decline to count votes cast for him. The hearing comes as Florida's Republican gubernatorial primary continues ahead of the Aug. 18 primary date.

cards.headline: Fentanyl summit in Orlando draws teens, DEA chief and families affected by synthetic opioid crisis
cards.teaser: Students from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined grieving parents and DEA Administrator Terrance Cole at the Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week.
cards.body:
Teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined grieving parents and federal law enforcement at the Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week. The students traveled from around the country to learn about the resurgence of fentanyl so they can return home with a message about one of the country's deadliest drug threats. Hannah Kahn, 18, who attended the summit, explained that fentanyl is often not recognized as a danger because people are not seeking it out directly. Kahn said it is just laced within other drugs. Jasmine Figueroa, 19, offered pointed advice for adults on how to talk to young people about drugs, stating that it is not a taboo topic and adults should tell them what cocaine is because they will get educated one way or another.

This year's summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a new partner. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole sat down with reporters to discuss the ongoing threat, stating that this poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels. Cole pointed to new tools from the current administration, noting that the president has designated Mexican cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for targeting them. Mari Rodriguez, whose daughter Imam died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023, described her grief. Rodriguez said her daughter made the mistake of buying a Percocet pill that had fentanyl in it, and it took her life. Rodriguez argued that work should have started in 2009, when the first fentanyl was found on streets.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance lowers homeowners rates by average of 5.6% for Florida customers
cards.teaser: Security First Insurance is reducing homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said all those savings the company is required to pass along to customers, and the company has been doing so. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year the deductible goes down 20 percent as long as the customer doesn't have a loss, Burt DeVriese said. Once a customer has a loss, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Premiums in South Florida generally run high, and online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

cards.headline: Everglades detention facility Alligator Alcatraz completely dismantled one month after closure announcement
cards.teaser: Alligator Alcatraz, which held undocumented immigrants in the Everglades for about a year, has been completely dismantled after Gov. Ron DeSantis announced last month it would shut down.
cards.body:
'Alligator Alcatraz' has been completely dismantled this week after Governor Ron DeSantis announced last month that the facility would be shut down. Aerial footage provided by WPLG showed the site, which had held undocumented immigrants in the Everglades for about a year, now sits empty. News broke in May that Alligator Alcatraz would soon close.

Maxwell Frost visited the facility on May 26 and told WPTV he saw clear signs that operations were winding down, including packed-up intake areas and a significantly smaller detainee population. The facility had detained roughly 1,500 people at a time during its peak. DeSantis said 21,000 detainees were deported through Alligator Alcatraz. On June 16, ICE confirmed that all detainees had been removed in preparation for hurricane season. Environmental groups are preparing to continue their federal lawsuit, arguing the state and federal governments still need to account for what was built, what damage was done and how the site will be restored.

hero.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks fosters and adopters during shelter renovation
hero.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation.
hero.body:
The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. In the meantime, the renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work. Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said the animals are really being affected by the sound of the construction, which is very loud and can be very stressful for an animal in a closed kennel.

About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

cards.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
cards.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
cards.body:
Martin County faces a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years. The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements, but only $701 million is currently available, meaning the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Of the $701 million currently available, all but $10 million comes from state and federal funding sources. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories through 2050.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. State Road 710 is among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns, with about $300 million in projects planned for the corridor.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast providing free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying residents in Martin County.
cards.body: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying residents in Martin County. A pool alarm is one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning, the coalition said. Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out a survey to determine eligibility. The alarms are available to Martin County residents with a residential pool, with one alarm per household and no income or priority group requirements. They are available while supplies last. A 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm but is not included, the coalition said. For more information, residents can call (772) 462-3501.

cards.headline: Jonathan Dickinson State Park concession closure leaves visitors without boats and tours
cards.teaser: Jonathan Dickinson State Park's concession operation is closed indefinitely this summer, leaving visitors without access to boat rentals, canoe rentals, and the popular Loxahatchee Queen tour to Trapper Nelson's Island.
cards.body:
Jonathan Dickinson State Park's concession operation is closed indefinitely this summer, leaving visitors without access to boat rentals, canoe rentals, and the popular Loxahatchee Queen tour to Trapper Nelson's Island. Park officials told WPTV the vendor who operated the concession had their contract expire. The park is now searching for a new vendor, but warns the approval process is lengthy and could take months.

Max Santos, a Jupiter local who has been coming to the park his entire life, said he and others were caught off guard when they arrived to find the concession office closed. Santos said the concession had allowed visitors to access bike rentals, canoes, motorboats, and tours, along with a place to get refreshments after activities. Daniela Sellitti drove from West Palm Beach with her kids hoping to take them on the Loxahatchee Queen to Trapper Nelson's Island, only to find the service unavailable. The park's website says the concession is closed indefinitely. Sellitti said it would be nice if the park is able to find a contract with someone else who will come in and open a concession and get the boats running again, so visitors can enjoy the river and get a chance to go over to Trapper Nelson's, which is a part of Florida history.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound couple is asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis, holding onto faith every step of the way.
cards.body:
Dave and Faren Motz met in South Florida before moving to Maui, where they married and raised their family. Faren raised all three of their kids and home schooled them, and the couple started a business with a farm where they served children. Years later, the couple moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer.

As the couple searched for the right healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource. Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid. Dave, a former firefighter, had long been the family's provider, but now Faren has stepped up to support them both. Doctors told Dave he has an 85% chance of recovery. Faren works at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show their support can stop by and visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on. The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: FDOT to Hold Public Workshops on Willoughby Boulevard Improvement Study
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Transportation will hold two public workshops to discuss proposed improvements along Willoughby Boulevard between Monterey Road and U.S. 1 in Martin Count
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Transportation will hold two public workshops to discuss proposed improvements along Willoughby Boulevard between Monterey Road and U.S. 1 in Martin County.

The meetings are part of a Project Development and Environment, or PD&E, study examining potential alternatives for the corridor. FDOT will offer the workshop in virtual and in-person formats, and each meeting will include a presentation followed by an opportunity for residents to ask questions and provide feedback.

## Virtual workshop scheduled for July 28

The virtual workshop will begin at **5:30 p.m. Tuesday, July 28.** Participants must register in advance at [https://tinyurl.com/Willoughby-APW](https://tinyurl.com/Willoughby-APW).

People who prefer to join by phone can call **1-469-423-0557** and enter access code 35124623#.

Registered participants will receive an email containing a link to join the meeting. Those attending from a mobile device will need the free Microsoft Teams application. FDOT recommends allowing enough time to log in before the presentation begins.

## In-person workshop scheduled for July 29

The in-person workshop will begin at **5:30 p.m. Wednesday, July 29,** at the 10th Street Community Center, 724 SE 10th Street, Stuart, FL 34994.

The meeting will use an open-house format. FDOT staff will be available to explain the proposed alternatives, answer questions and assist attendees.

Questions and comments will be addressed in the order they are received. If a question cannot be answered during the event, FDOT will provide a written response after the meeting. Residents may also submit questions or comments before the workshop by contacting the project manager.

## What the study will evaluate

A PD&E study is an early phase of the transportation planning process used to evaluate possible improvements and determine how a project could move forward.

The process typically considers traffic operations, roadway safety, environmental effects, community impacts, engineering needs and estimated costs. Feedback gathered during the workshops will help FDOT evaluate the proposed alternatives for Willoughby Boulevard.

## Accessibility accommodations available

Anyone requiring accommodations under the Americans with Disabilities Act should contact FDOT at least seven days before the meeting.

Accommodation requests may be directed to FDOT Project Manager Vanita Saini, P.E., at **954-777-4468** or [Vanita.Saini@dot.state.fl.us](mailto:Vanita.Saini@dot.state.fl.us). Written requests may be mailed to the Florida Department of Transportation, 3400 West Commercial Boulevard, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309.

People with hearing or speech impairments may contact the Florida Relay Service at 1-800-955-8771 for TDD service or 1-800-955-8770 for voice service.

For additional project information, contact Saini at 954-777-4468 or toll-free at 866-336-8435, extension 4468.

hero.headline: Dale Mincey charged with first-degree murder in shooting death of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Barnes
hero.teaser: Dale Mincey, 41, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in the fatal shooting of his uncle, 66-year-old Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes. Karen Moye, Barnes' sister, also faces charges for providing false information to investigators.
hero.body:
Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with Barnes' death, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said. Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes, 66, was taken to a local hospital, where he died. During questioning, Mincey told detectives he could not recall what happened the day of the shooting and that he didn't have any issues with Barnes and did not know how Barnes died, an arrest affidavit said. However, he admitted to owning two firearms.

Karen Moye was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police, an arrest affidavit said. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said Tuesday during a press conference that detectives uncovered information indicating that Moye, the victim's sister and mother of the suspect, knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to the homicide investigation. She has been charged with false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. Barnes leaves behind three adult children.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman claims $5 million lottery prize from scratch-off ticket bought on Okeechobee Road
cards.teaser: Maria Duran, 57, claimed a $5 million top prize from a scratch-off game on April 6 and chose to receive her winnings as a lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.
cards.body:
Florida Lottery officials announced Friday that Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The game's overall odds of winning are 1-in-2.90, but the chance of winning $5 million playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents return home after nearly two years following structural damage evacuation
cards.teaser: Some Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County are returning home after nearly two years of being displaced after structural damage in August 2024 forced evacuations from buildings 3, 4, and 5.
cards.body:
Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they were notified last month they could return to their condos after nearly two years of being displaced. Katie Johnson was the first to share with WPTV that residents had been told they could come back following an inspection in August 2024 that found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return and obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie described the work still underway at the property, saying crews are still moving the dirt back under the buildings. Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot.

Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia. Eric said the financial toll has been severe and that they had to drain all their savings accounts and 401ks just trying to make ends meet. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors like Eric Johnson who cannot return, saying she feels bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce neighbors pack planning meeting over Causeway Cove high-rise development proposal
cards.teaser: The Fort Pierce Planning Board reviewed the Causeway Cove development project Monday, which includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall off Seaway Drive.
cards.body:
Neighbors packed the chamber Monday as Fort Pierce's planning board reviewed the Causeway Cove development project off Seaway Drive. The project includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space. The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing.

Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area and take away from the beauty of the place. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic, saying nobody has thought this out and that there will be massive traffic jams with people unable to get on or off the island. City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved, stating the city does not have a play and has been eliminated from the process because it is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie couple fights rezoning of lot behind home near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive
cards.teaser: Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo are searching for answers after the Port St. Lucie City Council voted unanimously to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial, despite their months-long opposition.
cards.body:
The Mucciolos have called Port St. Lucie home for years, drawn to the property by its beautiful setting and backyard views of nature. In a unanimous vote, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved changing the lot behind their yard, where trees currently stand, to be rezoned from residential to commercial. The council says the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood. One council member said adding commercial closer to neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, which reduces overall traffic because trips are shorter. The Mucciolos have fought the rezoning for months and say their little piece of paradise is under threat, expecting it to be gone in six months or a year.

The two spoke at Monday's meeting, voicing their concerns, but they feel the council left them unheard and are now searching for answers about where to go from here. The council held its second reading Monday. While there was public comment, it was a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges, applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion. The Mucciolos say the process needs to change until it is logical, transparent, caring, and provides hope for people. They say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District extinguishes Ford F-250 fire on Florida's Turnpike near Mile Marker 175
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded to a vehicle fire Monday morning on Florida's Turnpike Northbound near Mile Marker 175, finding a fully involved Ford F-250 pickup truck on the shoulder.
cards.body: St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded to a vehicle fire Monday morning on Florida's Turnpike Northbound near Mile Marker 175. Firefighters arrived to find a fully involved Ford F-250 pickup truck on the shoulder of the interstate. Crews initiated an aggressive fire attack, bringing the fire under control while working alongside the Florida Highway Patrol to maintain a safe scene for motorists. Traffic was temporarily impacted as firefighters extinguished the fire and secured the scene. No additional vehicles were involved. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff deploys extra deputies to combat speeding on Midway Road, U.S. 1, Indian River Drive
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer by deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro said he has a family that drives on these roadways and cares about his loved ones and everyone else's loved ones, adding that he wants to make this a safer community. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break and placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said the county sees a lot of excessive speeding and most recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues described stopping a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, Rodrigues said his top speed recorded was 73 mph. In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK flights in September, cites low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. He added that the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He praised the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said the Boston route is performing well and seeing great demand.

The JFK to Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December. Dambeck said the door is not closed on the route returning in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The cancellation removes direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports for Treasure Coast travelers, who will need to use alternative airports or connecting flights to reach New York City.

cards.headline: Applications open for free and reduced-price school meals in Indian River County
cards.teaser: Families in Indian River County can apply starting July 15 for free or reduced-price meals for students during the 2026-2027 school year.
cards.body:
Families in Indian River County are able to apply for free or reduced price meals for students starting July 15. Students at six Indian River County schools can receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs. Other families in the district may still qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on household size and income criteria. Families are encouraged to complete one application per household to determine eligibility for free or reduced-price school meals.

Families need their child's Student ID number, their child's full formal name as listed in FOCUS, a valid email address, and internet access or the LINQ Connect mobile app. Families whose households receive Florida Medicaid benefits need their 10-digit Medicaid case number that begins with the number 1. Families can find their Florida Medicaid case number by logging into their MyACCESS account or looking at their Notice of Eligibility Review letter from the Florida Department of Children and Families. To apply, families must visit www.LINQConnect.com, sign in or create an account, and search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach. Families then add their students using their Student ID and formal name, click School Services at the top menu, and select Free and Reduced Meal Application. Families with questions about the meal programs can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director, at 772-564-5041 or shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org.
